Screen checkConfirm in Vanderbilt's Oracle or UKG during a recorded demo: Where the shared administrative calendar is published and who maintains it; Exact definitions of HCM Transaction Cutoff and Retro Change Cutoff, and that the Retro cutoff is about two business days earlier; Weekly/biweekly cutoff dates relative to UKG approvals.

1 · Intro

When to use it.

Payroll runs on fixed dates. Your transactions have to be submitted and approved before the cutoff, or they wait for the next cycle.

The payroll calendar is the source of truth for every date. Plan your hires, changes, and terminations around it.

Use this whenYou are planning when to submit a transaction, or you need to know whether a change will make this payroll.

2 · Walk through

How to use the calendar.

Check off each item as you read.

Watch-outs

  • Do not assume the 18th. Check the calendar every month, and especially in December.
  • Back-dated changes are retro changes and have the earlier cutoff.
  • Open item: confirm where the shared administrative calendar is published and who maintains it.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • Oracle: Overview of Payroll Definitions (opens in a new tab)
  • Oracle: Recalculate Payroll for Retroactive Changes (opens in a new tab)

HCM Academy job aid · Start Here

The Shared Administrative Calendar

Use when: You are planning when to submit a transaction, or you need to know whether a change will make this payroll. · System: Process

  1. Treat the payroll calendar as the source of truth.
  2. Know the exempt (monthly) cutoff.
  3. Know what drives weekly and biweekly pay.
  4. Watch the HCM Transaction Cutoff and the Retro Change Cutoff.
    • Retro changes have the earlier deadline.
  5. Submit early enough for approvals.
  6. Know what happens if you miss it.

Watch-outs

  • Do not assume the 18th. Check the calendar every month, and especially in December.
  • Back-dated changes are retro changes and have the earlier cutoff.
  • Open item: confirm where the shared administrative calendar is published and who maintains it.
